title: processkit-cli `wait --report-outcome` report
description: The `wait --run-id <id> --report-outcome` form prints one outcome object; `wait --all --report-outcome` prints one array of those objects after its snapshot barrier clears. A plain `wait` prints nothing at all. The report never changes `wait`'s exit code — a reported non-zero `code` is still exit 0 for the waiter, and the run's own outcome codes are never forwarded as the waiting process's status. The normative prose is docs/registry.md, "Waiting — `wait`"; the in-code source of truth is src/wait.rs. Validated against fixtures/schema/cli/wait.jsonl, and against the real binary's output, by tests/machine_output.rs.

oneOf.description: The aggregate report: one entry per target in stable snapshot order.

waitOutcome.description: How the awaited run ended, as far as the waiter could honestly establish. Null fields are always present rather than omitted, so a consumer never has to distinguish absent from unknown.

run_id.description: The run the waiter was asked about — echoed even when nothing could be established about it.

status.description: `reported` — the waiter observed the run live, then read its terminal `runner_exit` event from the JSONL locator the record published. `unknown` — it could not: it never observed the run live (an unknown or already-finished run id), the record published no locator, the runner died without a terminal event, or the stream could not be read. `unknown` is honest data, not an error: the exit code is unchanged.

code.description: The terminal `runner_exit` event's `code` — the exit code the run's own runner process returned (the child's code, or a reserved runner-band code). Null when `status` is `unknown`.

source.description: The terminal `runner_exit` event's `source` — why the runner exited (`child_exit`, `timeout`, `control_cancel`, …). Null when `status` is `unknown`. The vocabulary is deliberately not duplicated here: fixtures/schema/v1/schema.json's `runnerExit.source` is its single source of truth, and it grows additively (docs/schema.md, "Versioning").

child_code.description: The child's own exit code when it exited on its own; null for a runner-imposed ending, for a child that never produced one, and whenever `status` is `unknown`.

then.description: A reported outcome always names both the code and the source it read from the terminal event; only `child_code` may still be null there.

else.description: An unknown outcome fabricates nothing: all three outcome fields are null.
